Filter a correlation network with the triangulated maximally filtered graph

Source: R/tmfg.R
tmfg_network.Rd

tmfg_network() filters a correlation matrix to a sparse backbone with the triangulated maximally filtered graph (TMFG). The TMFG retains, for \(p\) variables, exactly \(3(p - 2)\) edges, chosen greedily to carry as much of the absolute correlation as possible while the graph stays planar and built from tetrahedra (four-variable cliques) (Massara et al., 2016).

Like other information-filtering networks, the TMFG keeps the strongest associations while imposing a fixed, interpretable structure. It shows which associations form the core of the correlation structure, without a sample-size-dependent selection rule. tmfg_network() builds the TMFG from raw data or a correlation matrix.

It returns the graph with the signed correlation of each retained pair as the edge weight; the edges are marginal correlations, not partial correlations. The structure that defines the graph is checked by certificate().

For a Gaussian graphical model with partial correlations on the TMFG graph use logo_network(); for an unfiltered correlation network use cor_network(). The graph is the one built by NetworkToolbox::TMFG().

Usage

tmfg_network(
  data = NULL,
  cor_matrix = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  cor_method = c("pearson", "spearman", "kendall", "auto"),
  na_method = c("pairwise", "listwise"),
  labels = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A numeric data frame or matrix with one row per observation. Not needed when cor_matrix is given.

cor_matrix

A correlation matrix to use instead of data; a covariance matrix is rescaled to a correlation matrix.

n

Accepted and ignored: the TMFG needs no sample size. It exists so that a call written for the other estimators, (cor_matrix = , n = ), also works here.

cor_method

Correlation computed from data: "pearson" (default), "spearman", "kendall", or "auto" (polychoric and polyserial correlations for ordinal items; see cor_auto()).

na_method

Handling of missing values in data: "pairwise" (default) or "listwise". See ebic_glasso().

labels

Optional node labels, one unique label per node of the network.

Value

A fitted network of class psychnet (psychnet) whose edge weights are the signed correlations on the retained edges. as.data.frame() returns one row per edge with columns from, to and weight; certificate() reports the structural check. The object also stores the TMFG graph as a logical matrix, including any retained edge of weight 0 (adjacency), its four-variable cliques and three-variable separators (cliques, separators; used by logo_network()) and the correlation matrix (cor_matrix). The sample size is recorded when the network is built from data and is NA with cor_matrix.

Details

The construction starts from the four variables with the largest sums of above-average absolute correlations, joined as a tetrahedron. It then adds the remaining variables one at a time, each time choosing the variable and the triangular face of the current graph for which the variable's summed absolute correlation with the face's three variables is largest, and joining the variable to those three. The result is a chordal planar graph with \(3(p - 2)\) edges, which tmfg_certificate() verifies.

The graph always has \(3(p - 2)\) edges, but a retained pair whose correlation is exactly zero has edge weight 0 and is therefore absent from as.data.frame() and from the printed edge count. With continuous data this happens only for a correlation matrix with exact zeros, such as a constructed or block-diagonal cor_matrix.

Conditions

psychnet_bad_input when there are fewer than four variables, cor_matrix is not a finite, symmetric, positive semi-definite matrix with a positive diagonal, an argument is invalid, or labels do not match the nodes; psychnet_constant_variable (warning) when a constant or all-missing column is dropped.

References

Massara, G. P., Di Matteo, T., & Aste, T. (2016). Network filtering for big data: Triangulated maximally filtered graph. Journal of Complex Networks, 5(2), 161-178. doi:10.1093/comnet/cnw015

See also

tmfg_certificate() and certificate() for the check; logo_network() for the Gaussian graphical model on this graph; psychnet(), which routes method = "tmfg" here; psychnet for the result.

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- matrix(stats::rnorm(200 * 6), 200, 6)
tmfg_network(x)
#> <psychnet> tmfg network
#>   nodes: 6   edges: 12   (undirected)
#>   structural certificate (violated TMFG invariants): 0
